problems.title: Watermelon (Codeforces 4A)
problems.description: Can a watermelon of weight w be split into two even, positive parts? A one-line condition using the % operator. Difficulty 800.

problems.title: Bit++ (Codeforces 282A)
problems.description: Apply n statements like X++ or --X to a variable and print its final value. Practises reading strings and a counter. Difficulty 800.

problems.title: Team (Codeforces 231A)
problems.description: Count the problems that at least two of three friends are sure about. Practises loops and summing values. Difficulty 800.

problems.title: Way Too Long Words (Codeforces 71A)
problems.description: Abbreviate words longer than 10 characters, e.g. "localization" becomes "l10n". Practises std::string, .size() and indexing. Difficulty 800.

problems.title: Next Round (Codeforces 158A)
problems.description: Count the contestants who advance to the next round. Practises arrays (or std::vector) and comparing elements. Difficulty 800.

exercises.title: Say "Hello, World!" with C++
exercises.description: Write and run your very first C++ program: include <iostream>, write int main() and print a line with std::cout.

exercises.title: Input and Output
exercises.description: Read three integers with std::cin and print their sum with std::cout. Practises the >> and << operators.

exercises.title: Basic Data Types
exercises.description: Read and print an int, long, char, float and double. Shows how each fundamental type stores and prints values.

exercises.title: Conditional Statements
exercises.description: Print a number's English name for 1–9, or "Greater than 9" otherwise. Practises if / else if / else chains.

exercises.title: For Loop
exercises.description: Loop over a range of numbers and print each one in words or as even/odd. Practises the for statement and conditions inside a loop.

exercises.title: Functions
exercises.description: Write a function max_of_four(a, b, c, d) that returns the largest of four integers. Practises declaring, defining and calling functions.

challenges.title: Intro to C++: First Steps
challenges.description:
Your first C++ programs, from printing a line to reading input and working with basic types.

Finish the three exercises, then solve Watermelon on Codeforces using what you learned.

challenges.title: Intro to C++: Decisions, Loops & Functions
challenges.description:
Put if statements, for loops and functions to work.

Start with the three guided exercises, then try the four Codeforces problems, roughly from easiest to hardest: Bit++, Team, Way Too Long Words, Next Round.

quizzes.title: Introduction to C++
quizzes.description: Five quick questions on the basics: program structure, I/O, types, constants and loops.

questions.question: Which header do you need to include to use std::cout and std::cin?
Every C++ program starts running from which function?
After int x = 7 / 2; what value does x hold?
Given const int n = 10; what happens if you later write n = 20;?
answers: n stays 10 and the line is ignored

questions.question: Which loop always runs its body at least once?

lessons.title: Introduction to C++
lessons.description:
Your first steps in C++, no programming experience needed (about 30 minutes). Write and run your first program, store values in variables, read input, make decisions with if, repeat with loops and split code into functions. Every example is a complete program you can copy and run.

After the lesson, try the "Intro to C++" challenges under Practice and the "Introduction to C++" quiz.
